newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA UNABLE TO SHAKE OFF BETIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA UNABLE TO SHAKE OFF BETIS.

text.p: Barcelona failed to gain any breathing space in the fight for Spain's second European Cup place despite a comfortable 3-0 win over struggling Compostela on Sunday.
Third-placed Real Betis stayed level on points with Barcelona after a thrilling 3-2 injury time victory over Atletico Madrid.
Both teams trail Real Madrid by six points. The leaders play Racing Santander on Monday.
Barcelona finally produced some of their best soccer of the season in a first half which was only five minutes old when Frenchman Laurent Blanc rose to head home his first goal for the club.

Bulgarian Hristo Stoichkov added the second from a superb through ball from midfielder Ivan de la Pena, and Brazilian prodigy Ronaldo knocked in the third after goalkeeper Francisco Falagan had blocked his 62nd minute penalty.
Barcelona's straightforward win contrasted with the cliff-hanger between Betis and reigning champions Atletico.
Atletico went ahead on the half-hour through Juan Eduardo Esnaider, but the fiery Argentine was sent off for butting an opponent shortly afterwards.
Betis striker Alfonso Perez volleyed home a superb equaliser before halftime and put his side ahead shortly after the break.
But an own goal scored during a defenisve mix-up seemed to have deprived the home side of two points before the international rounded off a memorable hat-trick in injury time.

Three points behind Barcelona and Betis are Deportivo Coruna, 3-0 winners over Oviedo with two goals from Brazilian striker Renaldo. Another Brazilian, Rivaldo once again turned in a fine performance to prove that he is more at home under compatriot Carlos Alberto Silva than former coach John Toshack.

Atletico are a further four points back, while sixth-placed Real Sociedad went down 1-0 to became the latest victims of a rapidly improving Extremadura side who have left the automatic relegation zone for the first time.
Once place ahead of Extremadura are Zaragoza, who scored their 2,000th league goal to go ahead at Athletic Bilbao, but needed a late strike to salvage a 2-2 draw.

The game was marred by an injury to Zaragoza's Austrian goalkeeper Otto Konrad caused by a firework thrown from the stands. Konrad was taken to hospital, but despite the initial scare had not suffered serious burns.
A 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano lifted Hercules off the bottom and above Sevilla, who went down 4-2 at Valencia on Saturday.
